summary: This is a 90-day execution plan for a biotech/research project (ARGUS) currently scored at TRL 2.75, outlining concrete deliverables, artifact requirements, and dates needed to achieve a higher TRL score in a MIRA re-assessment. The document maps MIRA criticisms to specific actions and artifacts, and defines a pre-registered primary endpoint around centriole age predicting cell division timing. The project is at an early stage (biology TRL 1, platform TRL ~3-4) with planned milestones running through March 2027.

content_blocks.title: Document Overview and Governing Rule
content_blocks.content: Title: 'Ninety-day execution plan — what turns 2.75 into a new score.' The document's governing rule: every line is either a deliverable with a date and an artifact, or a mapping from a criticism to the action that answers it. Nothing is a promise without a file behind it. The current TRL score is 2.75 and the goal is to raise it via a MIRA re-assessment by 1 March 2027.

content_blocks.title: Section 1: Deliverables Table
content_blocks.content:
Six deliverables with due dates, required artifacts, workstream assignments, and expected TRL effects:

1. Fiducial autofocus prototype mounted on the OpenFlexure fork | Due: 15 Jan 2027 | Artifact: Photo log, CAD revision, wiring note in hardware/ | Workstream: W2 | TRL effect: 3→4

2. 72h focus-hold test, drift plotted | Due: 20 Jan 2027 | Artifact: CSV of focus error vs time, plot, summary in docs/ | Workstream: W2 | TRL effect: closes P0 gap against Axio Observer

3. Protocol pre-registration deposited (OSF or Zenodo) | Due: before first imaging run | Artifact: DOI, timestamp, immutable version | Workstream: W1 | TRL effect: removes 'analysis can drift' objection

4. Unattended end-to-end run on fixed samples producing a tracked-division log | Due: 31 Jan 2027 | Artifact: machine-readable log, run config, error report | Workstream: W3 | TRL effect: 4→5

5. Second contributor onboarded (advisory or paid) | Due: 28 Feb 2027 | Artifact: name, role, signed scope, first commit or first review | Workstream: team | TRL effect: removes single-programmer objection

6. Re-assessment request with 1–4 attached | Due: 1 Mar 2027 | Artifact: request text + attachments | Workstream: all | TRL effect: new score

Note: 'If 1, 2 and 4 slip, the project-level TRL 1 stands and I do not contest it.'

content_blocks.title: Section 2: Primary Endpoint Definition (Pre-Registration)
content_blocks.content:
The primary endpoint must be numeric and locked before the first imaging run:

- Primary: Inherited centriole age rank predicts the interdivision interval in the same cell, tested by a pre-specified rank correlation with a stated effect-size floor; failure threshold fixed in advance.
- Secondary: Division-interval variance explained by centriole age after controlling for cell volume and birth time.
- Futility rule: If the first cohort shows no association above the floor, the hypothesis is reported as not supported in that system and the paper says so.

Key instruction: 'Do not tune the floor after seeing the data. That single sentence is what separates a pre-registration from a press release.'

content_blocks.title: Section 3: Criticism → Action → Expected Movement (Page 1)
content_blocks.content:
MIRA criticisms mapped to actions and document locations:

1. Criticism: 'Entirely prospective, TRL 1 for everything' | Action: Per-workstream table plus artifacts 1, 2, 4 | Where: §2 of the supplement, items 1–4

2. Criticism: 'Therapeutic relevance indirect' | Action: A validated division-timing readout, not a target claim; endpoint locked in item 3 | Where: §7 table, item 3

content_blocks.title: Section 3: Criticism → Action → Expected Movement (Page 2)
content_blocks.content:
Continued MIRA criticisms mapped to actions:

3. Criticism: 'Optionality aspirational' | Action: One intervention class producing a dose-ordered shift in division timing, second cell system post-pilot, next review | Where: post-pilot, next review

4. Criticism: 'IP 2/5, open licences' | Action: Method claims named, filing gate dated, cost line-itemed | Where: §4, gate at 60 days after positive pilot

5. Criticism: 'Small team, one programmer' | Action: Item 5, plus verified test count (29 — 12 pytest, 17 Rust, stated in the TRL evidence pack), frozen spec, written procedures, public upstream patch | Where: §5, team field answer

6. Criticism: 'No funding' | Action: OSC and Foresight pending, STF rejection declared with reason | Where: §5

7. Criticism: 'Low confidence' | Action: Artifact index; the missing input was files, not plan | Where: §3, attachments 1–4

content_blocks.title: Section 4: What Not To Do
content_blocks.content:
Strategic constraints explicitly stated:
- Do not ask MIRA to raise TRL for the biology. It is 1, and arguing otherwise destroys credibility.
- Do not claim the Caltech correspondence as a collaboration. It is correspondence.
- Do not resubmit to Sovereign Tech Fund before Q4 2027; the prevalence criterion needs adopters, not a better draft.
- Do not file a provisional on the readout method before the pilot threshold. A weak filing is worse than a defensive publication plus a dated gate.
- Do not add dimensions to the score by inflating team size. A second contributor with a signed scope beats five names.

content_blocks.content:

Test suite: 29 tests total — 12 pytest, 17 Rust (stated in TRL evidence pack). Caltech correspondence exists but is not a collaboration.
